title: An optimized method using peptide arrays for the identification of in vitro substrates of lysine methyltransferase enzymes
author: Rowe, Biggar

steps.title: Prepare membrane and synthesize peptides
steps.instruction: Synthesize peptide SPOT arrays on aminated cellulose membranes using Fmoc chemistry (e.g., Intavis ResPep SL) or prepare aminated cellulose membranes in‑house; after synthesis and deprotection wash the membranes six times with dichloromethane, then twice with anhydrous ethanol, and dry overnight in a desiccator before use.

steps.title: Spot peptides and block array
steps.instruction: Spot 1 µL of each substrate peptide (≈5 nmol per spot) onto a nitrocellulose membrane, allow the spots to air‑dry, block the array with blocking buffer for 1 h on a rocking platform at room temperature, wash once with TBS‑T for 5 min on the rocker, then store the array in TBS‑T at 4 °C or freeze at –20 °C for future use.

steps.title: Pre‑incubate array in buffer
steps.instruction: Submerge the blocked array in 6 mL methylation buffer (no [³H]SAM, no KMT) and incubate for 10 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Methylate array with radioactive SAM
steps.instruction: Replace the buffer with 6 mL fresh methylation buffer containing 0.466 µM [³H]SAM (specific activity 80 Ci mmol⁻¹) and 0.1–1 µM active KMT enzyme (typically 0.5 µM); seal the container with parafilm, rock at room temperature overnight, ensuring the array is fully submerged (volumes given for an 8.5 cm × 6 cm array; adjust for other sizes).

steps.title: Wash array and apply DPO enhancer
steps.instruction: Transfer the array to a labeled radioactive‑waste container; add 10 mL wash buffer, rock for 3 min at room temperature, then repeat the wash step five additional times (3 min each). Transfer the array with forceps to a container of anhydrous ethanol, submerge and rock for 2 min. Remove ethanol and add enough 7 % DPO solution (7 g 2,5‑diphenyloxazole dissolved in 100 mL ethanol, stored at room temperature) to fully submerge the array, agitate gently for 2 min, then dry the array on filter paper for ~3 h or overnight.

steps.title: Assemble cassette and expose film
steps.instruction: Place intensifying screens (Carestream BioMax TransScreen LE) on the inner bottom and inner cover of a radiographic cassette, wrap the dry array in a single layer of plastic wrap and insert it into the cassette; in complete darkness add a corner‑cut sheet of Amersham Hyperfilm MP, close the cassette, and expose at –80 °C for an initial 24 h (adjust exposure from hours to days based on enzyme activity).

steps.title: Develop radiographic film
steps.instruction: Develop the exposed film using the supplied developer and fixer according to the manufacturer’s instructions, performing all steps under safe light.

steps.title: Quantify spots using ImageJ
steps.instruction: Open ImageJ, install the ‘Protein Array Analyzer’ macro (download from https://imagej.nih.gov/ij/macros/toolsets/ if not already present), load the array image, open the Array Analysis menu and accept the default background correction, set the spot diameter appropriately, define the number of columns (nCol) and rows (nLin), mark the top‑left, top‑right and bottom‑left corners using the respective icons (they turn green when set), let the software outline the spots and adjust if necessary, then click the ‘Model’ button to obtain quantitative intensity data and a modeled image of the array.
